narrative.title: Longest Window of Metered Throughput
narrative.scenario: A metering gateway logs bytes moved per second as strictly positive counters, and the billing team needs the widest contiguous window whose total traffic equals a target quota exactly. Because every counter is positive, stretching a window can only increase its total, which the search may exploit.
narrative.inputFormat: An integer n, an array A of n positive integers, and an integer K, the target window total.
narrative.outputFormat: The number of seconds in the longest contiguous window whose total equals K, or 0 when no such window exists.

testCases.explanation: The windows [1,2], [3] and [1,1,1] all total 3, and the longest of them spans three seconds.
Only the trailing pair [2,3] reaches the quota, giving a window of length 2.

hintLevels: Level 1: Every counter is positive, so extending the window can only push its total up - that lets one window slide instead of restarting at each index.
Level 2: Grow the window by moving the right edge forward; while the total exceeds the quota, pull the left edge forward to shrink it.
Level 3: A quota larger than the sum of everything yields 0, and the window length must be measured as right minus left plus one whenever the totals match.
